problem: Most VLN methods discard navigation history after each episode, which is unrealistic in persistent environments. Recent methods that concatenate past trajectories with the current one add redundant observations that bring little information gain and even harmful noise.
motivation: In persistent environments, an agent's earlier trajectories hold useful information for later instructions. Using all of it indiscriminately hurts, so the agent needs to select only the relevant history.
key_idea: TraceNav selects relevant historical information during persistent navigation with multi-granularity matching: image-text matching to find target candidates in past observations, and instruction-trajectory matching to score how well each candidate's trajectory fits the instruction.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract suggests that selecting relevant history, rather than concatenating everything, removes redundant noise and improves navigation. It also suggests that coarse-to-fine matching works better than single-level retrieval.
method: Image-text matching: uses vision-language models and object detection models to identify target candidates in historical observations.
Instruction-trajectory matching: a cross-modal transformer infers how well each candidate's trajectory matches the text instruction.
Multi-granularity matching strategy: combines the two matching levels to select relevant history during persistent navigation.
History-traceable framework: uses the selected history to guide navigation toward the goal, evaluated in pre-exploration-like and iterative setups.
